title: Three Products and a Fourth
statement:
Real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfy
$$(a+1)(b+1)(c+1)=5,\qquad (a+2)(b+2)(c+2)=-3,\qquad (a+3)(b+3)(c+3)=4.$$
Find the value of $abc$.
hints: Don't try to find $a$, $b$ and $c$ individually. Look at the single function $F(x)=(x+a)(x+b)(x+c)$. The three conditions give its values at $x=1,2,3$, and $abc$ is its value at $x=0$.

Use finite differences on the values of $F(x)=(x+a)(x+b)(x+c)$ at $x=0,1,2,3$. This polynomial is a cubic with leading coefficient $1$, and the third difference of such a cubic is the same constant whatever its other coefficients are.

Write $F(x)=x^3+px^2+qx+r$ and check the combination $F(3)-3F(2)+3F(1)-F(0)$ term by term: the terms in $p$, $q$ and $r$ all cancel, and the $x^3$ terms leave $27-3\cdot 8+3\cdot 1-0=6$. Now put in the known values of $F(1)$, $F(2)$ and $F(3)$.
solution:
Let $F(x)=(x+a)(x+b)(x+c)$, a monic cubic, so $F(1)=5$, $F(2)=-3$, $F(3)=4$ and $F(0)=abc$.

The third finite difference of a monic cubic is $3!=6$, so
$$F(3)-3F(2)+3F(1)-F(0)=6.$$
Hence $4+9+15-F(0)=6$, so $F(0)=22$.
